task-memory-reference.purpose: Preserve aligned goal, slice, diagram, and memory context for long Compass-guided work when LLM context may be lost or compressed.

activation.rule: Do not create task memory for every task.
Create task memory for Compass-guided work that has developer-approved gated design context before implementation, even when the approved implementation has only one slice.
Gated design context includes brainstorming, align-context, evidence-discovery, fit-design, design, baseline-discovery, or delta-design outputs that the developer approved or selected.

Create task memory for long or risky work when the task type or discovered risk suggests meaningful checkpoint risk, such as new_feature, architecture_change, large refactor, or another task with at least two concrete slices.
Create or resume task memory after the developer and agent have aligned on the goal and design context, and before the first implementation slice starts.
If a task has no gated design context and only one implementation slice, do not create task memory unless the developer explicitly asks for it.

pre-implementation-gate.purpose: Make task memory impossible to forget once gated design context or long multi-slice work is aligned.
pre-implementation-gate.rule: Evaluate this gate after align-context, fit-design, or the approved design phase has produced approved context or implementation slices.
Implementation must not start until Compass reports one outcome: created, resumed, or not-required.
For created or resumed, report the task memory folder path and current active or first pending slice.
For not-required, report why there is no gated design context to preserve and why the work is below the long-work threshold.
If task memory is required but cannot be created or loaded, stop before implementation and report the blocker unless the developer explicitly overrides the gate.

If the target project is missing docs/_templates task memory files, use the installed Compass templates or this reference structure. Missing templates are a documentation gap, not a reason to skip the gate.

templates.preferred-source: docs/_templates/task-goal.md, docs/_templates/task-diagram.md, and docs/_templates/task-memories.md in the target project.
templates.fallback-source: assets/docs-seed/_templates/task-goal.md, task-diagram.md, and task-memories.md from the installed Compass skill.
Use the required file purposes, statuses, lifecycle, resume rules, and Mermaid rules in this XML when no template file is available.
templates.rule: Do not skip task memory because templates are missing.

required-headings.purpose: Compass-standard headings every project task template must keep. Projects may add, reorder, or rename anything else; the Compass templates are samples.
required-headings.heading: ## Non-Goals
## Success Criteria
## Slices
## Latest Evidence
## Goal Links
## How To Read
## Text Checkpoints
## SUMMARIES
## HISTORIES
required-headings.rule: scripts/docs-index.sh --tasks checks these headings in every task folder, plus the headings of the project's own docs/_templates/task-*.md when that template exists.

goal-statuses.status: The goal is currently in progress.
The goal is finished and verified.
The goal was replaced by a new goal.
The goal stopped without a replacement.

slice-statuses.status: The slice is planned but not started.
The slice is currently being worked on.
The slice is complete and verified.
The slice cannot proceed until a blocker is resolved.

file.name: goal.md
file.purpose: Source of truth for goal identity, status, description, approved scope, non-goals, success criteria, slice list, links to superseded or successor goals, and latest evidence.
file.rule: Update goal.md whenever the goal status, approved scope, slice list, slice status, blocker, successor link, or latest evidence changes.

Keep goal.md as current state only: replace Latest Evidence at each slice instead of appending, record per-slice evidence in memories.md HISTORIES, and move durable research findings to docs/modules or a decision record.
goal.md may carry optional Do and Don't sections. When the developer rejects an approach at a gate, record it as a Don't with the reason. Before acting against a Don't, ask the developer first.

A task folder may hold supporting files, such as contracts, schemas, fixtures, or long notes, with no line limit. List each supporting file in the goal.md References section with when to read it, and read a supporting file only when the current slice needs it.

A supporting file that stays the source of truth after the task, such as an API contract or schema the code depends on, moves to the project's durable location (docs/reference, docs/runbooks, or the code location the project uses) when the goal completes, and the task keeps a link. docs/.tasks may be ignored by git, so it must not hold the only copy of a shared artifact.

file.name: diagram.md
file.purpose: Human-readable checkpoint visualization using Mermaid plus text support.
file.rule: Include status legend and a text fallback so the checkpoint map remains readable when Mermaid is not rendered.
Update the Mermaid diagram whenever goal.md or memories.md changes slice or goal state.

file.name: memories.md
file.purpose: Summaries and reverse-chronological histories for context recovery.
file.rule: Keep SUMMARIES current with the latest compressed state.

Rewrite SUMMARIES at each checkpoint instead of appending, and keep it near 40 lines. Everything from SUMMARIES to the next heading defined by the project template is read on resume, so do not park detail sections there.

For gated design work, SUMMARIES must include approved brainstorming, align-context, and design outputs: selected slice, scope, non-goals, decisions, trade-offs, open questions, behavior or delta design, test matrix or verification plan, implementation slices, and approval evidence.
The LLM memikirkan field must contain a rationale snapshot, not private chain-of-thought.

lifecycle.event: Create all required files after align-context, fit-design, or approved design and before the first implementation slice.
Create or update task memory with the approved brainstorming, align-context, and design summaries before implementation starts.
Mark the slice active in goal.md, update diagram.md to blue, and add a memory history entry.
Mark the slice done in goal.md, record evidence, update diagram.md to green, and add a memory history entry.
Mark the slice blocked in goal.md, record the blocker, update diagram.md to red, and add a memory history entry.
If the goal remains stable, update the existing task folder instead of creating a new folder.
Create a new task folder, mark the old goal superseded, cross-link both goals, and record the reason in both memories.md files.
Mark the goal completed, record final evidence, and move supporting files that stay the source of truth to their durable project location.

resume.rule: At the start of a long Compass-guided task, run scripts/docs-index.sh --tasks to list open goals before creating a new task memory folder, instead of opening every goal.md.
If an active goal's updated date is more than 14 days old, offer to mark it completed or cancelled before selecting a goal.
Report docs-index.sh --tasks warnings as documentation gaps; do not rewrite existing task memory without developer approval.
If exactly one active relevant goal exists, load goal.md in full and the SUMMARIES section plus the newest HISTORIES entry of memories.md before planning or implementation.
Read older HISTORIES entries or diagram.md only when the summaries are not enough; diagram.md is the human-facing view of the slice state already recorded in goal.md.
If multiple active goals could match, ask one clarification question before choosing.
If an active goal conflicts with the user's new request, treat that as a potential goal change and ask before superseding it.

mermaid.rule: Use flowchart diagrams for checkpoint flow unless the user asks for another Mermaid type.
Use class definitions for pending, active, done, and blocked states.
Use short node labels and explain detail in surrounding text.
